nodes.characterization_summary: AXRD profiles show as-synthesized PtCu₃ film fitted to one peak; dealloyed Pt-Cu film fitted to two peaks. As X-ray energy approaches Cu adsorption edge, peak 2 (interior Cu-containing region) weakens while peak 1 (Pt surface) remains unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The AXRD profiles of the as-synthesized PtCu₃ film and dealloyed Pt-Cu film can be fitted to one peak and two peaks (peaks 1 and 2), respectively. As the X-ray energy approached the Cu adsorption edge, the (111) integrated scattering intensity for both as-synthesized PtCu₃ film and peak 2 of the dealloyed Pt-Cu film weakened ... peak 1 was ascribed to the Pt surface layer without Cu, and peak 2 was ascribed to the interior region with a certain content of Cu.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD used to evaluate out-of-plane tensile strain (ε_zz) on Pt films grown on SrTiO3 substrate based on peak position shifts; in-plane compressive strain (ε_xx) derived using Poisson ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) is a straightforward way for characterizing lattice strain. The incorporation of another metal with a dissimilar lattice constant results in the positive or negative shift of the peak position ... Temmel et al. proposed the evaluation of out-of-plane tensile strain (ε_zz) on Pt films grown on the SrTiO3 substrate based on the shift in XRD peak positions of Pt films.
